rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read of every pronoun/demonstrative/definite-NP in the body against prior-chunk history. Chunk 0 line 11 'The PR shipped and the ticket is closed' — session-artifact carve-out (the student's own prior-exercise PR/ticket). Line 11 'the next one'/'this one' = 'the session', same sentence. Line 13 'It'/'it' (x2) = `./CLAUDE.local.md`, named line 5 and start of same sentence. Line 15 'This file'/'this' = same file, named line 13. Chunk 1 line 21 'this is where they land on disk' = the rules file, established repeatedly by this point; line 23 blockquote 'the orient and introspect phases' resolves via BOTH the session-artifact carve-out (the student's own just-run session, per the compound-and-close-1 prompt's own 'Review this session end-to-end: the orientation and introspection...') and the module-arc-beat carve-out (`orient-and-introspect.md` is Ex1, run before this file per `getting-going.md` line 44 vs line 50 include order). Chunk 2 line 30 'Claude's summary'/'it misreads' = the retro output the chunk-1 prompt asked Claude to produce. Chunk 3 line 35 'it'/'That'/'it' all resolve within the same two sentences to CLAUDE.local.md and the .gitignore edit. Chunk 4 line 39 'the first compound pass' = chunk 1's action, named 'compound' throughout. Closest-to-violating candidate: chunk 4 line 46 'your rules files' (plural) — only one rules file is being WRITTEN in this exercise, but the deck has named a second, distinct rules-file concept by this point (chunk 0 line 13 'a team's rules and guardrails', echoed in the chunk-1 prompt fence's 'not the team ./CLAUDE.md'), so the plural resolves to that named personal+team pair rather than dangling with no candidate. Holds, but it is the one line in the file I would not call comfortably obvious on a first read.

No sentence in the body (lines 1-49) points at another file by position. The only backward references (line 11's PR/ticket) are session-artifact, not cross-file-by-position. No 'the opening lecture said' / 'earlier module' style phrasing anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 11: 'The PR shipped and the ticket is closed.' Verified against `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md` line 121: '...Ex2 (fix-tests-first) TDD bug fix, ship the PR → Ex3 (close-the-ticket) read the team's tracker conventions off one real ticket, close the bug's ticket...' — both referenced beats (PR shipped, ticket closed) currently exist as Ex2/Ex3 immediately before this file in the module's include order (lines 48, 50).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body; this exercise is a compound/retro loop, not a live-demo beat.

Smallest chunk is chunk 3 (lines 33-36): 'If `CLAUDE.local.md` wasn't already ignored, the compound step added it to your `.gitignore`. That is an uncommitted change now; commit it, or drop it.' A self-carrying instruction plus a decision the student must make, not a wait-state bullet. No chunk in the file is content-free.

Chunk 1 'Write your rules file from the session' -> body writes the rules file (lines 19-21, prompt at 25). Chunk 2 'Push back where the summary misreads' -> body pushes back on the summary (lines 30-31). Chunk 3 'Keep or revert the `.gitignore` edit' -> body does exactly that (line 35). Chunk 4 'Sweep the session into your rules file one more time' -> second-sweep prompt (39-44) plus the token-cost aside (46) and escape-hatch note (48), both about managing the resulting file. Chunk 0's H1 'Compound and close the loop' covers the whole lede (compounding, the rules-file choice, the bloat warning). No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

Checked all six sub-items against the full body. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. No anaphora/epistrophe triple — line 11's 'a test, a doc, a check' and line 13's 'one file, gitignored, read at the top of every session' are plain asyndetic lists, not repeated-clause-opening/closing rhetoric. No self-grading superlative (closest is line 9's '**The point:** every push-back is a hint toward your own rules' — a claim about the student's own action, not a rating of the exercise). No number-plus-retraction pattern (line 3's 'Time: 15 minutes' is a plain metadata field, not a hedged measurement). No abstraction-noun stacks — vocabulary stays concrete (tracker, ticket, scrollback, gitignore, tokens). No verb triplet with an empty leg. Ran `grep -nE 'Not [A-Za-z].*\. Not [A-Za-z].*\.' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--compound-and-close.body.txt` in this session -> 0 hits (exit 1, no match), confirming the first sub-item by direct grep in addition to the manual read of the rest.

Chunk 1's blockquote lead '**Long session, long read.**' (line 23) and chunk 4's '**The escape hatch is deliberate.**' (line 48) are one handle each, within the <=1 non-chrome budget per chunk. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two bullets add nothing over what the slide already holds. Chunk 1, line 20: 'You are not drafting from a blank page. The agent reads the session for you.' — restates line 19 ('Claude reviews the whole scrollback in one shot and drafts your rules from how you actually worked') from the student's vantage point; no new move/object/tell/priority, reassurance-as-restatement, class (a)'s shape at small scale. Chunk 2, line 31 second sentence: 'Born from the session, evolved over time.' — a closing flourish restating the 'the session is the evidence' theme already stated at chunk 0 line 11 and again by 'The rules file is yours now' in the same bullet; class (c) aphorism-kicker shape (closes the chunk by re-announcing a point already made, no new instruction). Neither reads as a curriculum-level LAW being re-announced, which is why this is filed non-blocking rather than as a blocking finding — the slide is still followable without either sentence, it just carries two lines that do no work.
